findings.title: ESP implicit match injected into shared flex-parser helper breaks other users
findings.explanation:
mlx5dr_definer_get_flex_parser_fc is a generic helper: it maps a flex-parser byte offset to a field. The IPv6 routing-extension conversion (shown at line 2579) calls it, and so does the eCPRI conversion. In non-relaxed mode the new block adds ESP matching for every caller.

eCPRI over Ethernet: no rule sets the outer IP_PROTOCOL, so the else branch forces ip_protocol == ESP. The rule can then never match real eCPRI frames.

eCPRI over UDP: IP_PROTOCOL holds udp_protocol_set, so the over_udp branch sets outer L4_DPORT to the IPsec NAT-T port when the user gave no dport. The rule then matches only UDP/4500 and misses eCPRI traffic.

SRH is mostly unaffected when it is not tunnelled, because its IP_PROTOCOL is already set. But the block always uses outer fields (inner=false) while routing_ext uses cd->tunnel, so for a tunnelled SRH it can still add an outer ESP/UDP-4500 constraint.

In short, matching that belongs to the ESP item is done in a helper that knows nothing about ESP.
findings.suggestion: Take the ESP ip_protocol / UDP-dport implicit matching out of mlx5dr_definer_get_flex_parser_fc. Put it in the ESP item conversion function (e.g. mlx5dr_definer_conv_item_esp), so it runs only for RTE_FLOW_ITEM_TYPE_ESP.
findings.evidence: /* To match on ESP we must match on ip_protocol and optionally on l4_dport */

findings.title: ESP-specific matching added to generic flex parser helper
findings.explanation: mlx5dr_definer_get_flex_parser_fc is shared by the IPv6 routing ext and eCPRI conversions. In non-relaxed mode the new code forces ip_protocol == ESP (or UDP dport 4500) for every caller. An eCPRI item whose IP protocol is not already set will wrongly match only ESP packets, so eCPRI rules break. The SRH caller is mostly unaffected because its IP_PROTOCOL is already set.
findings.suggestion: Move the ESP protocol/port setup into the ESP item converter, or gate it on an explicit parameter or item type.
